title: Numeric provider attachment IDs are coerced into integer indexes
reasoning: The public attachment input contract says attachment_id may be a provider ID or a numeric index string, and the service connector accepts either int or str. In inline attachment rendering, any string attachment_id made only of digits is converted to int before fetch_attachment. That changes the meaning of legitimate provider IDs like '12345' into positional indexes, which can fetch the wrong attachment or fail even though the provider ID was present in metadata.
reproduction: Use a connector that reports an attachment with attachment_id='12345' where the provider expects that string ID. mail_fetch(include_attachments='inline') converts it to integer 12345 before calling service.fetch_attachment.
recommendation: Do not coerce provider metadata IDs based solely on string contents. Preserve attachment_id as a string when it came from metadata; reserve integer indexes only for generated fallback identifiers or explicitly indexed user inputs.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were included for numeric-string provider attachment IDs or for distinguishing provider IDs from positional indexes.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a connector stub whose fetch_attachment records the identifier type and assert inline rendering passes '12345' as a string when that is the metadata attachment_id.
minimumFixScope: Adjust _render_attachments identifier selection so metadata attachment IDs keep their original type unless the code generated an index fallback.
